item.title: Visual Merchandising & Upstream Replenishment: The Logistics of Shelf Availability
item.description:
What are the Key Takeaways from this Executive Summary?

Quick answer

A display only works if the supply chain behind it can keep it full. That means the store plan, the warehouse layout, the way pallets are built and the delivery schedule all have to agree with each other. Where they do not, the shelf empties first and the reason sits three steps upstream.
  • Bridge the departmental divide: merchandising and supply chain teams often work separately, so a promotion launches before the stock behind it is in position.
  • Warehouse slotting matters: when the distribution centre is laid out against the store plan, picking takes less handling and restocking takes less time on the floor.
  • Pallet building decides store labour: a pallet sorted by aisle can be rolled straight to the floor. A mixed pallet has to be broken down in the stockroom first.
  • Forecasting supports OTIF: On-Time In-Full is the measure that tells you whether the display was supported. Read it per promotion, not as a monthly average.

Why is the Disconnect Between Visual Merchandising and Supply Chain Costly?

item.title: Managing Retail Promotional Peaks: Capacity, Cross-Docking, and Returns
item.description:
What are the Key Takeaways from this Executive Summary?

Quick answer

A promotional peak tests three things: whether you can get trucks, whether stock can cross the warehouse without being put away, and whether you can handle the returns that follow. Each one can be prepared before the peak. None can be fixed during it.
  • Cross-docking keeps fast stock moving. Instead of putting a pallet away and picking it again later, you move it straight from the inbound door to the outbound trailer.
  • Get spare carrier capacity agreed in advance. When your main carriers turn down loads, you need a second and third option already priced, not a phone call on the day.
  • Plan the returns before the peak, not after it. Returns arrive a few weeks behind the sales. If nobody has planned for them, they block the dock you need for outbound.

How Can Logistics Leaders Prepare for the Unpredictability of Promotional Peaks?
